clue.text: Duck swimming at the bottom in lake by reserve

parts.note: a sub is a reserve player in a team

indicators.note: one piece sits in the middle of the lake word, wrapped by its letters

parts.note: a mere is a small lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A duck paddles around on the bottom of a lake beside a nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird, but it is the verb meaning to push under water; 'by' just places the reserve alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone or something is to push it under water, plunge it below the surface.

clue.text: Join American next to bar

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
bar and but both mean except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: An American takes a seat beside the bar to join the drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub counter but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that abut share a border, meeting or touching along an edge, so the verb means join.

clue.text: Chart single?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to log or document something in writing
second meaning: a disc with one song on it, sold in shops

explanation.surface: It reads like asking whether a song released alone has made the pop charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words suggest the hit parade, but one is a verb for documenting and the other a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To chart progress is to document it in writing; a single is a vinyl disc carrying one song.

clue.text: Famous horrible person stripped snorting lines

indicators.note: something stripped has lost its outer covering, so both end letters go
a person snorting something takes it inside, so the other piece goes within

parts.note: a bastard, a nasty person, without its first and last letters
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A nasty celebrity is caught naked snorting lines of cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: The horrible person is a common swear word for a nasty man; 'lines' suggests cocaine, but it is just the abbreviation L twice.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast is one made up entirely of celebrated, well-known performers.

clue.text: Overplays clear hits across both sides of album

indicators.note: one piece stretches across the other, with a letter either side
to clear something out empties its middle, leaving only the shell

parts.note: this word with its middle cleared out

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A band's obvious hit singles are spread across both sides of the LP.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor exaggerates; as a verb, to ham is to act in an overdone, theatrical way.

clue.text: Come to show's opening with known hits

parts.note: an idea that comes to you strikes you

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of this word
a secret that is out is generally known

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at a show's opening night along with its well-known songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hits' looks like songs but is the verb defined; 'Come to' means occur to, as a thought does.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike out is to lash out, swinging a blow at somebody, so it means hits.

clue.text: Celebrated: eat out with no starter when entertaining over

indicators.note: a dish with no starter has lost its first course, so the opening letter goes
a host entertaining a guest holds them inside the house

parts.note: a picnic is a meal eaten outdoors, minus its first letter
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A celebrity dines out, skipping the first course while hosting cricket's end of an over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' is not a restaurant meal but PICNIC; an over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is so widely recognised and admired that it has become a famous symbol.

clue.text: Silent call that might get picked up

parts.note: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak
to give someone a bell is British slang for a phone call

explanation.surface: A silent phone call that someone might pick up and answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests answering the phone, but the gym weight is lifted. 'Give me a bell' is British for 'ring me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short bar with weights on each end is lifted repeatedly in the gym for exercise.

clue.text: Dry air essentially in air-conditioned room

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the abbreviation for cooled air

parts.note: AC is short for air-conditioning, wrapped round the rest
TT means teetotal, someone who stays dry

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre, the middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of this word

explanation.surface: The air feels dry inside an air-conditioned room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' means not drinking alcohol, abbreviated as TT for teetotal; TT and I go between the A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room built into the space just beneath the roof of a house.

clue.text: Issue of magazine looking back

indicators.note: something looking back faces the opposite way, so read the word from its end

parts.note: Time is a well-known American news magazine

explanation.surface: A retrospective issue of a magazine, looking back over past events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' seems to be a noun for an edition, but it is the verb to send out.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit light or a sound is to issue it, giving it out or sending it forth.

clue.text: Fixed ideas round band's leader with periods in studio

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of this word
recording sessions are periods spent in a studio

explanation.surface: A band's frontman has a fixed idea about how many hours to spend recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessions are thoughts that grip the mind and will not let go, ideas that stay fixed.

clue.text: One holding camera to mostly hear music player

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to try a case is to hear it in court, minus its last letter
the iPod was Apple's portable music player

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a camera while listening to music on a portable player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the legal sense: a judge tries or hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged stand is what a photographer mounts a camera on to keep it steady.

clue.text: Drink a shot over two forms of pop

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means flipped upward, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a nip is a small shot of spirits
cola is fizzy pop and da is a word for dad, also called pop

explanation.surface: Ordering a drink: a shot of spirits plus a couple of fizzy sodas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' does double duty: soft drink and father, giving COLA and DA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pina colada is a cocktail of rum, pineapple juice and coconut cream.

clue.text: Became excited after joining in for feeling

indicators.note: excited letters jump about and settle in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
the little word in, joined on to the end

explanation.surface: Someone got thrilled after signing up for a feeling of belonging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After joining in' tells you to add the word in to the end of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The ambience of a place is its atmosphere or mood, the feeling it gives visitors.

clue.text: Finally succumb, call dentist: one's called initially after the filling?

definitions.text: one's called initially after the filling?

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each word that follows

parts.note: last letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Giving in and phoning the dentist about a filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' suggests a tooth, but it is the contents of a sandwich: bacon, lettuce and tomato, named by their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: This sandwich is named by the initial letters of its three ingredients, bacon, lettuce and tomato.

clue.text: Rest on this: take pulse first

indicators.note: first says that the pulse piece is placed at the front

parts.note: a bean is a pulse, an edible seed
to bag something is to take or seize it

explanation.surface: A doctor's instruction: rest here, but take the patient's pulse first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' is not a heartbeat but an edible seed such as a lentil or bean.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanbag is a soft floppy seat filled with beads, something you sit or lounge on.

clue.text: Musical instrument's part for greatest hit-maker?

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the nearby words is taken, sitting inside them

parts.note: taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A part played on a musical instrument for a great hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greatest hit' suggests a chart song, but Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest and hit people for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxer Muhammad Ali billed himself as The Greatest, and boxers land punches on opponents.

clue.text: Flash with these skirts in sexiest costumes

indicators.note: the skirts of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters of this word
robes are costumes or ceremonial garments

explanation.surface: Someone flashes the skirts in a show of the sexiest outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' looks like clothing among costumes, but it means edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobe lights produce rapid bursts of bright light, flashing on and off at a nightclub.

clue.text: Broadening the mind with tablet: I find heartless guy when drunk

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with its heart gone a word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of this word

explanation.surface: Someone takes a pill, gets drunk and claims the experience is mind-expanding.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the drug ecstasy, a common crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edifying improves you morally or intellectually, an instructive experience that enlarges your thinking.

clue.text: Travelling in Britain? Hit road after playing

indicators.note: after places the remaining pieces behind the word for performing

parts.note: a show that is on is being performed or playing

indicators.note: something that is hit gets knocked about into a new arrangement

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Britain, as on car stickers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A band playing in Britain decides to hit the road on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit road' reads as setting off on a journey, but hit stirs the road letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers on board a ship, train or plane are travelling in it, carried as part of its load.

clue.text: Learning without advanced development

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: education is the process of learning
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Learning that comes with no advanced development or progress.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare word: eduction is the act of drawing out or bringing forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Eduction means drawing out or eliciting something latent, a bringing forth that resembles development.

clue.text: Make love on date: I like that thing

parts.note: to do something is to make it
love is a score of nothing in tennis, which looks like O
D is the abbreviation for date
ah is an exclamation of pleasure, saying I like it

explanation.surface: Someone proposes making love on a date and says they'd like that thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make love' splits into two words: make and love, which is zero in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodah is a casual word for a thing whose name you can't remember, like thingummy or whatsit.

clue.text: Early lousy form? Briefly possessing dope

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse, its earliest form
with means possessing, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: An early draft was lousy, apparently written by someone who was on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lousy' is literal here: belonging to a louse. 'Dope' is not drugs but a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly or stupid person, a fool or idiot, just as a dope is.

clue.text: Horny being in Girls Aloud: idol primarily after love

indicators.note: after places the initials behind the score word

parts.note: love is a zero score, nil

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of each of these words

parts.note: first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A randy fan of the pop group Girls Aloud idolises them out of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' means having horns, not lustful; Girls Aloud were a British girl band.
explanation.definitionFit: The nilgai is a large Indian antelope; the males carry short horns, so it is a horned creature.

clue.text: It might remove business title at work retaining old list

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, keeping the other letter inside
letters at work are busy moving about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
a roll is a list of names, as in roll call

explanation.surface: An office tool might strip a business of its title while keeping an old list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business' is a euphemism for what one does in the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavatory paper wipes away what one leaves after doing one's business, a jokey euphemism.

clue.text: Stage rotating on it

indicators.note: rotating turns the words round so the letters run the opposite way

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolving stage with a performer standing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' is a level or step, not a theatre platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or rank in a series, one step or stage in a graded system.

clue.text: Fish in light streams

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flat sea creatures related to sharks
second meaning: narrow beams of light shining out

explanation.surface: Fish swimming in sunlit streams of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light streams' looks like gentle brooks but means beams of sunlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates and mantas are flat cartilaginous fish; sunbeams are narrow lines of light.

clue.text: 28 occasionally come down

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: the odd letters of the answer to 28 across, REALIGNS

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the stuff will come down every now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the answer at 28 across; its first, third, fifth and seventh letters give this.
explanation.definitionFit: When it rains, water drops come down from the clouds, falling from the sky.

clue.text: Go off drink over two days

indicators.note: one piece spreads over the other, covering it on both sides

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
D is the abbreviation for day, doubled

explanation.surface: Someone goes off drinking for a two-day bender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' is not leaving but turning bad, as an egg does.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that addle become rotten, so the verb means to spoil, turn bad or rot.

clue.text: Once more lines up a single for release after end of tour

indicators.note: after places the shuffled words behind the final letter
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of this word

indicators.note: letters released are set loose to fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A band lines up another single for release once their tour ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign something is to arrange it into a straight line again, putting it back in order.
